name: Haytham Hussein
tagline: Electrochemistry, materials science, and sustainable technologies for a circular economy.
introduction: Leading independent research at the University of Nottingham on conductive diamond electrochemistry, critical element recovery, and sustainable manufacturing.
bio: Haytham Hussein is an AXA Research Fellow in the Department of Chemistry at the University of Nottingham. He leads an independent research programme focused on engineering conductive diamond electrochemical cells for recovering critical and rare earth elements from batteries and electronic waste.

His work spans electrochemistry, advanced materials, microscopy, data science, and sustainable manufacturing. He uses green solvents, deep eutectic solvents, ionic liquids, and bioelectrochemistry to support circular-economy technologies, alongside teaching, postgraduate supervision, and academic leadership.

Before his current fellowship, Haytham held research positions at the Universities of Aberdeen, Swansea, Southampton, and Warwick. He also brings industrial experience from Procter & Gamble and Chemanol Petrochemicals, connecting rigorous research with process engineering, quality, and product development.
